FAILURE TO PROSECUTE Zuko Nonxuba

By: Tarryn Crossman | Commission

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
It’s an investigation that started in 2022 and went on for over a year. Finally, after Carte Blanche pushed and pushed, Zuko Nonxuba was struck from the roll in December 2024. It was a damning judgment with enough evidence to get a warrant issued for his arrest on 22 counts of fraud and theft. Months later, he remains at large. For nearly four years, fraud cases against him have dragged through the courts in East London and Mthatha. With one magistrate recusing herself after watching Carte Blanche’s exposé, while in Mthatha, another magistrate died in a car crash before handing down a verdict, and the retrial was dismissed under Section 147.
Meanwhile, the children he defrauded are still without justice, and the millions in court-awarded payouts that were paid over to Nonxuba have vanished. While the children are now dying.


Further information:
Where is Zuko now?
• Struck from the roll-on 4 December 2024 – judgment was damning.
• Warrant for arrest issued on 19 December (22 counts of fraud and theft, SIU cases).
• Months later, still not arrested. At large.
• After Months of looking for him, he is stopped at passport control coming into the country, but the NPA ordered him to be released as they were not happy with the charge sheet.

East London – justice delayed
• 3 fraud cases dragging on for almost 4 years.
• March 2025: Magistrate Twanet Olifair recuses herself after watching Carte Blanche exposé. Says she can’t remain impartial.
• Hawks claim they “couldn’t locate” him – even though he was meant to be in court. No plan made to arrest him there.
Mthatha – justice denied
• Magistrate dies in car accident before handing down verdict.
• Case retried, same evidence, same modus operandi as East London cases, yet case was acquitted.
The victims
• Thandiswa Xhanti’s son Ahlumile: awarded R13 million in 2020. Paid into Nonxuba Inc trust account. Never reached her.
• In 2023, Carte Blanche was the first to break the news to her – money gone.
• Her case used in striking him off – hard evidence of theft.
• Her son died last month. No money was ever awarded to him


Key questions
• Why is Nonxuba still free months after a warrant was issued?
• Why are the NPA and courts handling the same evidence so differently?
• How long must the children and families wait for justice or compensation?
